     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# user-invoked-harness.bats: does `disable-model-invocation: true` hide a
     4	# command from the model's Skill tool? (FR-8, SDD D-8.4)
     5	# =============================================================================
     6	# One live `claude -p` run in a throwaway project holding two fixture commands:
     7	# `fixture-hidden` (flagged) and `fixture-visible` (control, unflagged). The
     8	# live run gets the Skill tool only, so it cannot read the fixture bodies or
     9	# run anything else, and it never sees a real Loa command.
    10	#
    11	# Outcomes of the live test:
    12	#   pass   the control ran (its marker reached the stream) and the hidden
    13	#          command did not (no Skill tool_use for it, or an error result,
    14	#          and its marker is absent everywhere)
    15	#   fail   the hidden marker reached the stream: the flag does not hide the
    16	#          command, so FR-8 is lint-only and G-7 partial
    17	#   skip   no `claude` on PATH; LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0; CLI error, timeout or
    18	#          unparsable output; or the control never ran (inconclusive)
    19	# Set LOA_HARNESS_OUT=<file> to keep the raw stream-json as evidence.
    20	# The classifier is also exercised offline against canned streams.
    21	
    22	HIDDEN_MARK="HIDDEN-RAN"
    23	VISIBLE_MARK="VISIBLE-RAN"
    24	
    25	# classify_stream <stream-json file>
    26	# Prints one of: verified | flag-does-not-hide | inconclusive-control | unparsable
    27	classify_stream() {
    28	    local stream="$1"
    29	    if ! jq -e -s 'length > 0' "$stream" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    30	        echo "unparsable"
    31	        return 0
    32	    fi
    33	    # Marker text anywhere in a tool result, an injected user message or the
    34	    # final result means that command's body was loaded into the session.
    35	    local hidden_seen visible_seen
    36	    hidden_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$HIDDEN_MARK" \
    37	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    38	    visible_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$VISIBLE_MARK" \
    39	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    40	    if [[ "$hidden_seen" == "true" ]]; then
    41	        echo "flag-does-not-hide"
    42	    elif [[ "$visible_seen" != "true" ]]; then
    43	        echo "inconclusive-control"
    44	    else
    45	        echo "verified"
    46	    fi
    47	}
    48	
    49	# skill_calls <stream-json file>: one line per Skill tool_use, "<name>\t<is_error>"
    50	skill_calls() {
    51	    jq -r -s '
    52	      ([.[] | select(.type == "user") | .message.content[]? | select(.type? == "tool_result")
    53	         | {key: .tool_use_id, value: ((.is_error // false) | tostring)}] | from_entries) as $res
    54	      | .[] | select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]?
    55	      | select(.type? == "tool_use" and .name == "Skill")
    56	      | "\(.input.skill // .input.command // .input.name // "?")\t\($res[.id] // "no-result")"' "$1"
    57	}
    58	
    59	write_fixture_project() {
    60	    local dir="$1"
    61	    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude/commands"
    62	    git -C "$dir" init -q
    63	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-hidden.md" <<'EOF'
    64	---
    65	name: fixture-hidden
    66	description: fixture
    67	disable-model-invocation: true
    68	---
    69	
    70	Reply with the single word HIDDEN-RAN
    71	EOF
    72	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-visible.md" <<'EOF'
    73	---
    74	name: fixture-visible
    75	description: fixture
    76	---
    77	
    78	Reply with the single word VISIBLE-RAN
    79	EOF
    80	}
    81	
    82	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    83	# Offline: the classifier over canned streams (always runs)
    84	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    85	
    86	@test "classifier: hidden refused, control ran -> verified" {
    87	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/ok.jsonl"
    88	    cat > "$s" <<'EOF'
    89	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t1","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"fixture-hidden"}}]}}
    90	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"t1","is_error":true,"content":"Unknown skill: fixture-hidden"}]}}
    91	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t2","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"fixture-visible"}}]}}
    92	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"t2","content":"Launching skill: fixture-visible"}]}}
    93	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reply with the single word VISIBLE-RAN"}]}}
    94	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","result":"VISIBLE-RAN"}
    95	EOF
    96	    run classify_stream "$s"
    97	    [ "$output" = "verified" ]
    98	    run skill_calls "$s"
    99	    [[ "$output" == *$'fixture-hidden\ttrue'* ]]
   100	    [[ "$output" == *$'fixture-visible\tfalse'* ]]
   101	}
   102	
   103	@test "classifier: hidden body reached the stream -> flag-does-not-hide" {
   104	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/leak.jsonl"
   105	    cat > "$s" <<'EOF'
   106	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t1","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"fixture-hidden"}}]}}
   107	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reply with the single word HIDDEN-RAN"}]}}
   108	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","result":"HIDDEN-RAN VISIBLE-RAN"}
   109	EOF
   110	    run classify_stream "$s"
   111	    [ "$output" = "flag-does-not-hide" ]
   112	}
   113	
   114	@test "classifier: control never ran -> inconclusive-control" {
   115	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/noctl.jsonl"
   116	    cat > "$s" <<'EOF'
   117	{"type":"result","subtype":"error_max_turns","result":""}
   118	EOF
   119	    run classify_stream "$s"
   120	    [ "$output" = "inconclusive-control" ]
   121	}
   122	
   123	@test "classifier: garbage output -> unparsable" {
   124	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/bad.jsonl"
   125	    printf 'not json at all\n' > "$s"
   126	    run classify_stream "$s"
   127	    [ "$output" = "unparsable" ]
   128	}
   129	
   130	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   131	# Live: one claude -p run against the fixture project
   132	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   133	
   134	@test "live harness: disable-model-invocation hides a command from the Skill tool" {
   135	    if [[ "${LOA_HARNESS_CHECK:-1}" == "0" ]]; then
   136	        skip "LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0"
   137	    fi
   138	    if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   139	        skip "claude CLI not on PATH"
   140	    fi
   141	    if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   142	        skip "jq or timeout missing"
   143	    fi
   144	
   145	    local proj="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
   146	    write_fixture_project "$proj"
   147	    local out="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stream.jsonl"
   148	    local prompt="Use the Skill tool to invoke the skill named fixture-hidden, then use the Skill tool to invoke the skill named fixture-visible. Follow whatever each skill tells you, and report each tool result verbatim."
   149	
   150	    local rc=0
   151	    ( cd "$proj" && env -u CLAUDECODE timeout 180 claude -p --max-turns 3 \
   152	        --tools Skill --output-format stream-json --verbose \
   153	        --no-session-persistence "$prompt" ) > "$out" 2>"$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stderr" || rc=$?
   154	    if [[ -n "${LOA_HARNESS_OUT:-}" ]]; then
   155	        cp "$out" "$LOA_HARNESS_OUT"
   156	    fi
   157	
   158	    local verdict
   159	    verdict="$(classify_stream "$out")"
   160	    echo "verdict=$verdict rc=$rc" >&3
   161	    skill_calls "$out" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/skill_call: /' >&3 || true
   162	
   163	    case "$verdict" in
   164	        unparsable)
   165	            skip "CLI error or unparsable output (rc=$rc): $(head -c 300 "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stderr")" ;;
   166	        inconclusive-control)
   167	            skip "inconclusive: control not invocable (rc=$rc)" ;;
   168	        flag-does-not-hide)
   169	            echo "flag does not hide the command: FR-8 is lint-only, G-7 partial" >&2
   170	            return 1 ;;
   171	        verified)
   172	            return 0 ;;
   173	    esac
   174	    echo "unknown verdict: $verdict" >&2
   175	    return 1
   176	}

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/check-round-independence.bats
     4	#
     5	# tools/check-round-independence.sh reads the `<!-- round: N; questions: [...] -->`
     6	# blocks that `interview.pacing: rounds` puts at the end of every round
     7	# (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing) and fails
     8	# when a question depends on another question of the same round, on one never
     9	# asked earlier, when ids repeat without "reasked", or when rounds average
    10	# fewer than --min-average new questions (final round exempt).
    11	# =============================================================================
    12	
    13	setup() {
    14	    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    15	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    16	    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-round-independence.sh"
    17	    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/rounds"
    18	    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/transcript.md"
    19	}
    20	
    21	# Write a transcript whose rounds are the given JSON arrays, in order.
    22	transcript() {
    23	    local n=0 arr
    24	    : > "$T"

content.content:
{
  "status": null,
  "model": null,
  "verdict": null,
  "rejected_summary": null,
  "keys": [
    "findings",
    "metadata",
    "verdict_quality"
  ]
}
---FINDINGS
- [BLOCKING] (?)  — Rejecting a proposed replacement permanently prevents agents from proposing another replacement for the original decision.
- [BLOCKING] (?)  — Import commits ledger rows before performing fallible reference rewrites, without recording an import identity for safe retries.
- [BLOCKING] (?)  — op_confirm only refuses on live_run_signal (RUNNING state, fresh marker, env vars), but then calls derive_attribution 0, which checks the broader is_unattended. is_unattended also fires on the 'prd' signal (a PRD whose **Status** line contains 'autonomous' or 'unattended'). In that state derive_attribution silently drops --answer-ref with a WARN and REF becomes empty, so the confirm jq sets .decided_by = .proposed_by (typically 'agent') instead of 'operator', while the transition says by: operator:decisions-command. decisions.md rule 3 states the cli: ref is what records decided_by: operator. The same inconsistency makes op_reject on a decided row die with 'the context is unattended' for the operator whenever the PRD status says autonomous, even with no run active.
- [BLOCKING] (?)  — import copies every row of the pending file into the live ledger after only a schema validation (validate-artifact.sh --type decisions) and PEND-id rewriting. It never checks row status, decided_by, decided_by_ref or transitions. A pending file is agent-authored (the header says 'written outside the main checkout') and can trivially contain status: decided, decided_by: operator, or status: superseded rows. verify_and_swap treats all imported ids as 'touched', so its invariants do not catch this. This bypasses the stated invariant that 'a row becomes decided only' through /decisions confirm, which is the core trust property of the ledger.
- [ADVISORY] (?)  — The operator-only guard is `[[ "$(o recorded-by)" == decisions-command ]]`. disable-model-invocation only stops the Skill tool from launching /decisions; the model can still run `dec-write-lib.sh confirm --recorded-by decisions-command ...` through Bash, and the Karpathy/autonomous-agent docs now actively steer agents toward dec-write-lib.sh. The bats grep over command/skill bodies does not constrain runtime behaviour. The design text ('an agent that could run them would confirm its own decisions') therefore overstates the guarantee.
- [ADVISORY] (?)  — A non-operator supersede records supersede_proposed_by on the decided row and refuses any further supersede while that field is set. But op_reject never clears supersede_proposed_by on the old row when the proposed replacement is rejected, and op_confirm only consumes it on confirm. After one rejected replacement, the decided row is permanently locked against agent-proposed supersedes ('a replacement is already proposed'), and the dangling pointer references a rejected row.
---ADVISORY
---REJECTED
0 grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-rejected-review.jsonl

echo "===== A3: PRD Status autonomous -> operator confirm with cli: ref"; bash $D new --summary p1 --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by t --source s --status proposed --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$ALT" --quiet; printf '# PRD\n**Status:** Draft (autonomous run)\n' > grimoires/loa/prd.md; bash $D confirm --id DEC-0001 --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:2026-10-19T10:00:00Z --answer-ref cli:2026-10-19T10:00:00Z 2>&1 | tail -3; yq -o=json '.decisions[0] | {status, decided_by, decided_by_ref, by: .transitions[-1].by}' $L
echo "===== A3b: operator reject of a decided row under PRD autonomous"; bash $D reject --id DEC-0001 --rationale no --follow-up bd-1 --recorded-by decisions-command 2>&1 | tail -2; rm grimoires/loa/prd.md
echo "===== A1: reject a proposed replacement, then try another agent supersede"; bash $D new --summary p2 --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by t --source s --status proposed --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$ALT" --quiet; bash $D confirm --id DEC-0002 --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:2026-10-19T10:00:00Z --answer-ref cli:2026-10-19T10:00:00Z --quiet 2>/dev/null; bash $D supersede --id DEC-0002 --summary r1 --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by run-mode --source s --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$ALT" --quiet; bash $D reject --id DEC-0003 --rationale bad --follow-up bd-2 --recorded-by run-mode --quiet; echo "DEC-0002 supersede_proposed_by=$(yq '.decisions[1].supersede_proposed_by' $L) DEC-0003 status=$(yq '.decisions[2].status' $L)"; bash $D supersede --id DEC-0002 --summary r2 --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by run-mode --source s --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$ALT" --quiet 2>&1 | tail -1
echo "===== A4: import a pending file with a fabricated decided row"; mkdir -p grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-9; cat > grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-9/decisions-pending.yaml <<'EOF'
schema_version: 1
decisions:
  - id: PEND-0a1b2c3d
    created_at: 2026-10-19T09:00:00Z
    updated_at: 2026-10-19T09:00:00Z
    phase: implementation
    category: scope
    summary: fabricated decided row
    decision: d
    rationale: r
    alternatives_considered: [{option: x, rejected_because: y}]
    consequences: null
    proposed_by: agent
    decided_by: operator
    decided_by_ref: cli:2026-10-19T09:00:00Z
    evidence_sha256: null
    recorded_by: run-mode/sess
    commit: deadbeef
    source: s
    cycle: null
    supersedes: null
    supersede_proposed_by: null
    status: decided
    transitions:
      - {at: 2026-10-19T09:00:00Z, from: null, to: proposed, by: "agent:run-mode", evidence: s}
      - {at: 2026-10-19T09:00:00Z, from: proposed, to: decided, by: "operator:decisions-command", evidence: cli:2026-10-19T09:00:00Z}
    rejection_rationale: null
    follow_up: null
    prior_requests: []
EOF
bash $D import --from grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-9/decisions-pending.yaml 2>&1 | tail -2; yq -o=json '.decisions[-1] | {id, status, decided_by}' $L
echo "===== M2: decide an open row that already carries a decision"; bash $D new --summary o1 --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by t --source s --status open --decision d0 --rationale r0 --alternative-json "$ALT" --quiet; id=$(yq '.decisions[-1].id' $L); bash $D decide --id "$id" --decision d1 --rationale r1 --alternative-json "$ALT" --evidence e --recorded-by t 2>&1 | tail -2
echo "===== M3: help output tail"; bash $D --help 2>&1 | tail -2
echo "===== M35: list md with no rows for decided/agent"; bash $D list --status decided --voice agent --format md

## Overall Assessment

The sprint lands the decision ledger writer (`dec-write-lib.sh`), its fail-closed validator (`validate-artifact.sh --type decisions`), the operator-only `/decisions` command and allowlist, a default-off session-start surface, the round-independence checker, and the `rounds` interview pacing. I ran those suites against a merged tree (framework `.claude/` plus `pr/head/`). Every one of them is red on the PR as shipped, because the PR never adds the `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` file that the writer, the validator tests and the `.gitignore` negation all presuppose. ## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality: the tracked ledger the PR depends on is not in the PR

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:271` — every live-ledger write dies with `ledger not found: ... (restore the tracked grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml)` because no file at that path is added by the change; the writer has no init path and the docs forbid hand edits.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:271`, `head/.gitignore:150`, `head/tests/unit/validate-artifact.bats:643-646`, `head/tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:13`, `head/tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:28`, `head/tests/unit/grimoire-index.bats:80`
**Issue:** The diff lists 39 files; `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` is not one of them, yet `.gitignore:150` re-includes it "the decision ledger is tracked team state", `dec-write-lib.bats:12` says "the live ledger is seeded in the main checkout", and three test files `sed` the live file's header. On the merged tree every test in `dec-write-lib.bats` (44/44) and the decisions block of `validate-artifact.bats` and `grimoire-index.bats` fail in `setup`:
```
not ok 1 dec-write new: ids allocate max+1 and print DEC-%04d
# sed: can't read .../grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml: No such file or directory
not ok 6 validate-artifact decisions: the live ledger passes
```
With a header-only ledger seeded, all of them pass, so the gap is the missing artifact, not the code. Downstream, `validate_prd` (`head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:773-778`) then treats every cited DEC row as missing, so an unattended PRD that follows the new `[ASSUMPTION decision] (DEC-NNNN)` rule fails validation on a fresh checkout.
**Why This Matters:** The feature is unusable and its own suites are red on any clone until someone hand-creates the file the writer says never to hand-edit. CI for this PR cannot be green.
**Required Fix:** Add `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` (header comment starting `# grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml: the decision ledger`, `schema_version: 1`, `decisions: []`) to the change, or give the writer an explicit `init` that creates it (and have the tests not depend on the live file's header). Say in the report which it is.

### 2. Security / trust boundary: `import` lets an agent-authored pending file mint `decided` rows

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:642-647` — `op_import` copies every pending row verbatim after only a schema validation, so a pending file carrying `status: decided`, `decided_by: operator` and a forged `operator:decisions-command` transition lands in the live ledger as a decided row without `/decisions confirm`.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:627`, `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:642-647`, `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:686`
**Issue:** The header (`:12-18`) and `/decisions` (`head/.claude/commands/decisions.md:22-28`) state that a row becomes `decided` only through the operator command. `op_import` never checks `status`, `decided_by`, `decided_by_ref` or `transitions[].by` of the imported rows; `verify_and_swap` treats all imported ids as touched (new rows are allowed), and the validator's only guard for a new operator row (`:686`) fires solely while a live unattended signal holds. Reproduced on the merged tree with a hand-written pending file:
```
$ dec-write-lib.sh import --from grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-9/decisions-pending.yaml --quiet
PEND-0a1b2c3d DEC-0001
$ yq -o=json '.' decisions.yaml | jq -c '.decisions[-1] | {id,status,decided_by,decided_by_ref}'
{"id":"DEC-0001","status":"decided","decided_by":"operator","decided_by_ref":"cli:2026-10-19T09:00:00Z"}
$ validate-artifact.sh --type decisions --file decisions.yaml
INFO: 1 decision rows        (exit 0)
```
The pending file is written in agent worktrees by design (`:20-22`), and the "lead" who imports it is itself an agent session.
**Why This Matters:** This is the ledger's central trust property. CWE-284 (Improper Access Control) / CWE-345 (Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity): the attribution the whole feature exists to make trustworthy can be forged by the party it is meant to constrain.
**Required Fix:** In `op_import`, refuse (or normalise) any row whose `status` is not `open|proposed`, whose `decided_by`/`supersede_proposed_by` is not null, or whose transitions contain anything other than a single `null -> open|proposed` by `agent:*`/`flatline:*`/`dissent:*`. Mirror the rule in the validator for pending files (`$pending`) so the check is fail-closed on both sides, and add a negative test.

### 3. Functionality / attribution: a PRD `**Status**` line naming an autonomous run misattributes the operator's confirm and blocks the operator's reject

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:313-316` — `derive_attribution` drops `--answer-ref` whenever `is_unattended` holds, and `is_unattended` includes the `prd` signal (`:177-180`), while `op_confirm` (`:509`) only refuses on *live* signals; so an interactive operator confirm with `--answer-ref cli:...` while the PRD says "autonomous" records `decided_by: agent`.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:313-316`, `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:509-513`, `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:537-538`, `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:575`, `head/.claude/commands/decisions.md:54-56`
**Issue:** `/decisions` rule 3 says the `cli:` ref "is what records `decided_by: operator`". Reproduced with `grimoires/loa/prd.md` containing `**Status:** Draft (autonomous run)` and no run state, marker or env signal:
```
$ dec-write-lib.sh confirm --id DEC-0001 --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:... --answer-ref cli:...
dec-write: WARN: unattended context: --answer-ref ignored (...)
dec-write: confirmed DEC-0001
$ dec-write-lib.sh list --status decided --voice agent --format md
| p1 (DEC-0001) | agent | decided | r | s |          <- decided_by is agent
$ dec-write-lib.sh reject --id DEC-0001 --rationale no --follow-up bd-1 --recorded-by decisions-command
dec-write: reject: DEC-0001 is decided and the context is unattended; the operator rejects it interactively
```
The transition row says `by: operator:decisions-command` while the row says `decided_by: agent`, and the operator cannot reject a decided row at all for as long as the PRD keeps that status line (which an autonomous `/plan` leaves behind). The test at `head/tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:354-366` confirms without `--answer-ref`, so it never asserts `decided_by` in this state.
**Why This Matters:** The feature's purpose is to answer "which decisions did a human take?". Here the human's answer is silently filed as the agent's, and the operator's correction path is closed.
**Required Fix:** Make the two gates agree: either `op_confirm`/`op_reject(decided)` use the same `live_run_signal` test as the refusal (and `derive_attribution` takes a flag to honour the ref when the caller is the operator command), or drop the `prd` signal from `is_unattended` for operator calls. Add a test that confirms with a `cli:` ref under a PRD-only signal and asserts `decided_by: operator`.

### 4. Functionality / state machine: rejecting a proposed replacement locks the original decision against any further agent supersede, permanently

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:600-602` — the agent path of `op_supersede` refuses while `supersede_proposed_by` is set, but `op_reject` (`:560-587`) never clears that pointer on the old row when the proposed replacement is rejected, and the validator's append-only rule (`head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:681`) only allows `supersede_proposed_by` to move from null to a value, so no writer operation can ever clear it.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:600-602`, `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:580-583`, `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:681`
**Issue:** Reproduced: DEC-0002 decided; agent `supersede --id DEC-0002` creates DEC-0003 (proposed); `reject --id DEC-0003` succeeds; then
```
DEC-0002 supersede_proposed_by=DEC-0003 DEC-0003 status=rejected
$ dec-write-lib.sh supersede --id DEC-0002 ... --recorded-by run-mode
dec-write: supersede: a replacement is already proposed for DEC-0002: DEC-0003
```
The old row now carries a dangling pointer to a rejected row, and the validator (`:656-657`) accepts that shape, so the ledger stays "valid" while being wrong. Only the interactive operator path can still supersede.
**Why This Matters:** Reject-then-repropose is the normal correction loop in an unattended run; after one rejection the agent can no longer propose a replacement, and the only remedy violates the append-only rule.
**Required Fix:** On `reject` of a row with `supersedes` set, clear (or null out) `supersede_proposed_by` on the superseded row in the same write when it names the rejected row, and let the validator's content-edit exception (`:681`) permit that transition (`supersede_proposed_by` value -> null when the named row's new status is `rejected`). Add a test for reject-then-supersede.

content.text:
Review of sprint-1 is complete. Verdict: **CHANGES_REQUIRED**.

**What I did.** Read all 39 files in the PR, ran the adversarial cross-model review on the diff (two voices, zero rejected payloads), built a merged tree and executed the PR's own bats suites, and reproduced every blocking finding by hand before counting it. Feedback is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md` with a consistent LOA-VERDICT trailer (verdict-derive passes, with and without the envelope). The task brief's one-line-per-finding form is at `review.md` in the repo root.

**Blocking findings (4 high, all reproduced):**
- **The ledger file is missing.** The writer dies "restore the tracked grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml", the .gitignore negation re-includes it, and three test files read its header, but the PR never adds it. All 44 writer tests and the validator and index decision tests fail in setup on a clean clone. With a header-only ledger seeded, all 107 tests I could run pass.
- **`import` mints decided rows.** A hand-written pending file with `status: decided` and a forged operator transition lands in the live ledger and passes validation, bypassing the "decided only via /decisions confirm" invariant.
- **PRD-only unattended signal misattributes the operator.** With a PRD status line saying "autonomous", an interactive operator confirm with a `cli:` ref records `decided_by: agent`, and the operator cannot reject a decided row at all.
- **Reject leaves a permanent supersede lock.** Rejecting an agent-proposed replacement leaves the old row's pointer set; further agent supersedes are refused, and the append-only validator forbids clearing it.

**Non-blocking:** import is non-idempotent on a failed rewrite, `decide` on a pre-filled open row aborts with a misleading content-edit error, no CHANGELOG or PROCESS.md update for a new command, the report has no AC verification or test evidence, plus four low items (help output, list footer, redundant .gitignore pair, hard-coded flag day).

**Not run:** `agents-md-gen.bats` (needs the repo root files) and the live `claude -p` harness test. `br` is absent, so no beads comments were recorded. Next step is `/implement sprint-1` to address the four changes, then re-review.

**What I did.** Read all 39 files in the PR, ran the adversarial cross-model review on the diff (two voices, zero rejected payloads), built a merged tree and executed the PR's own bats suites, and reproduced every blocking finding by hand before counting it. Feedback is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md` with a consistent LOA-VERDICT trailer (verdict-derive passes, with and without the envelope). The task brief's one-line-per-finding form is at `review.md` in the repo root.

**Blocking findings (4 high, all reproduced):**
- **The ledger file is missing.** The writer dies "restore the tracked grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml", the .gitignore negation re-includes it, and three test files read its header, but the PR never adds it. All 44 writer tests and the validator and index decision tests fail in setup on a clean clone. With a header-only ledger seeded, all 107 tests I could run pass.
- **`import` mints decided rows.** A hand-written pending file with `status: decided` and a forged operator transition lands in the live ledger and passes validation, bypassing the "decided only via /decisions confirm" invariant.
- **PRD-only unattended signal misattributes the operator.** With a PRD status line saying "autonomous", an interactive operator confirm with a `cli:` ref records `decided_by: agent`, and the operator cannot reject a decided row at all.
- **Reject leaves a permanent supersede lock.** Rejecting an agent-proposed replacement leaves the old row's pointer set; further agent supersedes are refused, and the append-only validator forbids clearing it.

**Non-blocking:** import is non-idempotent on a failed rewrite, `decide` on a pre-filled open row aborts with a misleading content-edit error, no CHANGELOG or PROCESS.md update for a new command, the report has no AC verification or test evidence, plus four low items (help output, list footer, redundant .gitignore pair, hard-coded flag day).

**Not run:** `agents-md-gen.bats` (needs the repo root files) and the live `claude -p` harness test. `br` is absent, so no beads comments were recorded. Next step is `/implement sprint-1` to address the four changes, then re-review.
